_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: Dropsuite takes the reseller Authentication Token (X-Access-Token) plus X-Reseller-Token on GET /users, GET /users/{id} and /users/generate_support_sso_link, and ONE organization's authentication_token (returned by GET /users) on every other route. --org <id|owner email|external_id> resolves that token for organization-scoped commands; DROPSUITE_ORG routes requests that still carry the reseller token (MCP typed tools) through orgRoutingTransport; the fleet commands build one client per organization. Organization tokens stay in memory, are held by the shared credential kit as a declared response field (credkit-wiring), and never reach the local store (an organization-scoped read never writes through to it).
handfixes.why: Vendor REST reference (NinjaOne SaaS Backup REST API, sources/dropsuite-rest-api-subreseller-v1.00.pdf): 'User's Authentication token' vs 'Admin Token'. Without the routing every backup-data command 401s with the reseller token. Hand files internal/cli/dropsuite_org.go and dropsuite_routing.go (carried from the 4.33.5 print); the two transports are installed by the one ordered client hook in ds_guard.go, above the origin pin. Tests: internal/cli/dropsuite_fleet_test.go, TestOriginPinUnderEveryDropsuiteTransport, the dsblackbox battery (accounts/onedrives/sharepoint with --org, MCP with DROPSUITE_ORG).

handfixes.summary: The eight fleet commands (health, coverage, billing, evidence, hygiene, locate, drift, restore-test) are hand-written over the generated client; health snapshots and the restore-test ledger live in the local store's ds_* tables.
handfixes.why: Novel features of the first print (research 20261015-014520-278ea5bd), carried unchanged into the 4.34.2 render. A reprint that re-stubs a novel file shows here.

handfixes.why: Press template text does not fit a two-header, organization-scoped, read-only API. Re-applied by tools/fix_docs.py after every generate, dogfood and shipcheck; the auth narrative is fixed at its source (research.json).

An unresolved template pins nothing (every request refused).
handfixes.why: Work order host pinning. originPinTripper and the same check FIRST in CheckRedirect (hand file internal/cli/ds_guard.go), installed directly above the credential kit's transport (client.OutboundGuard) by the ONE client hook, so the organization routing, the redaction transport and the routing's organization-list loads all send through it (init order across files is not relied on). Tests: TestOriginPinRefusesRedirectToAnotherHost (reseller and routed organization token), TestOriginPinUnderEveryDropsuiteTransport, TestNormalizedOriginRefusesNonASCIIAndFillsPorts, TestRedirectNeverReachesAnotherHost (black-box, CLI and MCP).

handfixes.summary: The on-disk response cache is off on every client: GET /users bodies carry every organization's authentication_token and never sit in cache files.
handfixes.why: Work order: nothing but the credential store holds a credential. c.NoCache = true in guardClient (ds_guard.go); TestOriginPinUnderEveryDropsuiteTransport asserts it.

handfixes.summary: Every MCP tool that can change Dropsuite state previews and sends only with confirm: true (boolean). Dropsuite's only state changes reachable here are the portal sign-in link calls (each invalidates the previous link): the endpoint tools portal_get-login-link and organizations_get-support-sso-link preview their request; locate and evidence run as reads and preview without --sso-link / --with-sso-link unless confirmed. Fail closed: any other tool that is neither read-only nor a reviewed local-only command is gated too.
handfixes.why: Work order: every MCP write previews and sends only with confirm: true. Press 4.34.2 registers both sign-in link endpoint tools with no confirm. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/ds_confirm.go), called from RegisterTools after RegisterAll; only boolean true sends and confirm is never forwarded. Tests: TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm (also fails on any ungated non-read-only tool outside the reviewed local list), TestEndpointWriteToolPreviewsWithoutConfirm, TestMCPWritesNeedConfirm and TestMCPPreviewCannotBeTurnedOffByAnArgument (black-box: no link minted before confirm). Codex review round 1 class read-call-reaches-a-mint-route: a read-only tool whose path argument names a sign-in link route (organizations_get id generate_redirect_link, with DROPSUITE_ORG) minted a link; the client now marks a call it issues as a mutation (client.go doInternal: cliutil.MarkMutation) and the innermost API transport (ds_guard.go checkRoute) lets only a marked request reach any generate_* route in any spelling (format suffix, case, redirect hop) and refuses any path segment the API could route elsewhere (slash, backslash, percent, semicolon, dot or empty segment); the refusal is terminal (client.go terminalTransportRefusal), never retried. TestReadsNeverReachASignInLinkRoute and TestNoReadReachesASignInLinkRoute (black-box, CLI and MCP), seen failing first: r1-read-call-reaches-a-mint-route-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: billing --invoice (a local PSA CSV the operator names) is never an MCP argument: the billing command carries mcp:read-flags invoice, so the mirror drops it from the tool schema and refuses a call that supplies it by name before the companion CLI runs. The CLI opens it with os.Open(filepath.Clean(path)), no inline suppression.
handfixes.why: msp-skills check_mcp_file_flags.py (taint analysis over the connector) found the --invoice value reaching the companion CLI from a tools/call (work order P1 class: host file read from an MCP tool argument); check_security_gate.py then blocked the inline #nosec G304 on the open (no fleet precedent for hand code). Test TestBillingInvoicePathIsNotAnMCPArgument (seen failing first: r0-host-file-read-seen-failing.log); the fleet gate check_mcp_file_flags passes on the stage.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel and store scrub. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (DROPSUITE_ACCESS_TOKEN and DROPSUITE_RESELLER_TOKEN sent as X-Access-Token and X-Reseller-Token, DROPSUITE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN sent nowhere, GET /users authentication_token a response field bound to the API origin) and Files, which names config.toml, the legacy config, each explicit config with its 0600 credentials.toml and the global store under every --home, --config, DROPSUITE_HOME and DROPSUITE_CONFIG, and shows the kit the resolved https://{host}/api base through DROPSUITE_BASE_URL until AfterStart restores it (an unresolved template allows no origin). Each main starts with credkit.Start and credwire.AfterStart and ends with credkit.Exit; the MCP server runs credkit.MCPTools outermost and serves stdio through credkit.MCPIn and credkit.MCPOut. The API, streaming, probe, feedback and --deliver webhook clients go through credkit.Transport (client.OutboundGuard, below the origin pin); every SQLite handle opens through internal/credsql (credkit.SQLDriver, the MCP sql value cap as a DSN setting); every file write goes through the kit except the 0600 credential store and the config file (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, the declared exemption); children start through credkit.RunCommand and StartCommand; terminal checks use credkit.Terminal; auth set-token holds its stdin token with credkit.Hold.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Closes the three classes the factory print left open, each proven on the built binaries and seen failing on the pre-kit tree: credential-source-not-held (a DROPSUITE_CONFIG file with a multi-line literal before a broken line, and one with the token after its first MiB), secret-in-startup-diagnostics (the store refusal warning naming a home path that holds the token, CLI and MCP) and held-value-in-an-undecoded-encoding (quoted-printable over base64 over quoted-printable). Retired, reason replaced by the shared credential kit: secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, network-sinks-withheld.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal, the templated-base hand-off and the kit-wrapped SQLite driver.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes GET /users with the reseller pair (X-Access-Token and X-Reseller-Token) and reads the answer by status, calls a 404 a wrong base URL naming DROPSUITE_HOST and DROPSUITE_BASE_URL, names DROPSUITE_BASE_URL on a placeholder base URL, and, when the default host dropsuite.us is in force and the probe does not verify there (401, 404, no answer), keeps the api row negative and names DROPSUITE_HOST and DROPSUITE_BASE_URL, instead of calling any HTTP response reachable and printing 'present, not verified'.
handfixes.why: check_doctor_truth.py failed every state on the 4.34.2 print (issue #282): a working credential read 'present, not verified', a base URL at a web UI read 'reachable (HTML body at /)', expired, healthy and wrong-base gave one identical credentials verdict, and the harness's placeholder state (no base URL set, so https://{host}/api with the default host dropsuite.us) read 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)' without naming DROPSUITE_BASE_URL. Ported from the fleet form (prtg, cisco-umbrella) and adapted: GET /users is the one argument-free read that takes the reseller credential (every other one takes an organization token, and the generate* routes mint sign-in links), its body carries organization tokens so the probe discards it, and dropsuite.us is a real partner API host, so it is probed, never refused; only its remedy changes, because a partner on another Dropsuite API host gets a 401 or no answer there. doctor_verdict.go carries the replay recipe's helper signatures and no doctorBaseURLIsShippedPlaceholder, so replay_handfixes.py wires the probe, the no-credential row and the placeholder row but not the shipped-template refusal; doctorNameDefaultHost is wired by hand. Tests: doctor_verdict_test.go (seen failing first) and check_doctor_truth.py --slug dropsuite.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing (Origin, bearer, bounded body read), then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the refusal it decided.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it, and a bearer holding the refusal's text would get a piece of itself back.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the kit-wrapped handler.

handfixes.summary: dropsuite-mcp carries the press 4.34.2 token-protected streamable HTTP mode (--transport http, --addr, --tls-cert, --tls-key): DROPSUITE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN of at least 32 characters required, Authorization: Bearer checked on every request, a non-loopback Origin refused unless DROPSUITE_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS lists it, TLS required for any non-loopback bind, every response through credkit.MCPHTTP. stdio stays the default.
handfixes.why: The 4.34.2 render of this spec emitted a stdio-only main, so remote agents had no supported path and the runtime proof (verify-msp-skills feature 3) had nothing to drive. main.go and http_auth_test.go are the press 4.34.2 template as the other kit adopters carry it (mimecast's copy, slug names substituted), so the reviewed template shape is unchanged.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Declare the http transport in the spec's MCP config so the press emits this main natively.

asserts.contains: transport := flag.String("transport", defaultTransport(), "MCP transport: stdio | http")

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).
